amendment.basis: One bounded review round on the first preregistration commit (fbcca8f9), by claude-opus and gpt-6-astra reviewers, before any provider call. The arms, task, labels, batching, bounds, margin, bootstrap and billed-token definition are unchanged; the command, the call handling, the usage policy and the cost comparison changed as below.

changes.finding: decide() dropped A0 from the ranking when some of its usage was unknown, so a costlier candidate could be recommended, and the documents called interrupted calls neutral while they made an arm unrankable.
changes.change: A candidate is recommended only when its cost is strictly below A0's. Unknown A0 usage makes A0's cost a lower bound: a candidate below it is still recommended, otherwise the result is inconclusive_control_usage_incomplete. Which calls leave usage incomplete is stated once (metrics.usage_completeness).

changes.finding: An outage, an expired sign-in or a rate limit failed every batch twice within minutes, consumed each retry, and the run still exited 0.
changes.change: A call without a completed turn is unavailable: it never uses a retry, the UNAVAILABLE note stops every arm and the run exits 4. unbounded_connection_retries is off, so an outage fails a call instead of hanging it until the timeout. A finished arm with a failed batch exits 6.

changes.finding: The committed command still offered web search, a shell and sub-agents, and nothing detected tool use.
changes.change: Isolation overrides measured by isolation-probe/; any tool item in a call's session record or --json stream fails the call (tool_use), so no reply produced with a tool is scored.

changes.finding: The host's global AGENTS.md, skills and hooks reached every call, and Codex's session files for a call lived outside the private state directory.
changes.change: Each call has its own CODEX_HOME in its attempt directory, holding only a link to the native auth.json, a scratch HOME, TMPDIR and working directory outside the state tree, and an allowlisted environment; a run refuses while a system Codex configuration file exists.

changes.finding: analyze.py never verified the frozen inputs, so changed analysis or scoring code could produce a recommendation.
changes.change: analyze.py verifies every frozen input before reading anything and records the map in the decision file.

changes.finding: The LIMIT note was published after the call ended and after its slot was released, and a limit seen only by a runner that died was never published.
changes.change: A state-wide launch gate orders every call start after any stop note; the LIMIT note is published as soon as the event appears, before the slot is released; the arm's next run publishes an unpublished limit before any call.

scope_source: Coordinator task of 2026-09-26, which reports the user's request to maximize use of the GPT-6 family cleanly, with the token-save practice as the base layer. This plan records that scope and runs nothing; it does not itself establish approval to spend the shared allowance.
question: For a mechanical, deterministically scored extraction stage, which GPT-6 family member and reasoning effort matches gpt-6-astra at max effort (today's default for every GPT-6 step) at lower token cost, so that mechanical stages can route to it and the shared weekly allowance does more work?

host.codex_slot_pool: Three fcntl.flock slots (slot-1 to slot-3) in the host's shared Codex lock directory, which the landscape-sweep runner (tools/sota-convergence/landscape-sweep/codex_job.py) also takes. run_arm.py receives that directory as --lock-dir and never creates it, so a mistyped path is refused instead of starting a private pool.
host.observation_scope: Read-only facts seen while planning. Each run checks the Codex version, the inputs and the layout again and relies on nothing here.

isolation.why: The committed command offered the model web search, a shell and sub-agents (review of 2026-09-26, and the probe below), none of which a mechanical extraction needs, and any of which could reach data outside the prompt or add a second model to an arm.
isolation.measured: isolation-probe/probe.py ran codex-cli 0.157.1 on 2026-09-26 against a loopback fake Responses provider (isolation-probe/fake_tool_calls.py) inside a private network namespace, with no credential and a fresh CODEX_HOME per case. With the committed options, the first request offered functions[exec, wait, request_user_input, request_user_input_async], clock[sleep] and collaboration[followup_task, interrupt_agent, list_agents, send_message, spawn_agent, wait_agent]; a scripted web.run call sent a search request, and a code-mode exec cell listed the nested tools apply_patch, clock__curr_time, create_goal, exec_command, get_goal, update_goal, view_image, web__run and write_stdin and ran exec_command pwd. With -c features.multi_agent=false alone, the collaboration tools were still offered (case multi-agent-feature-off). With the overrides, for gpt-6-astra, gpt-6-sol and gpt-6-luna alike, the first request offered only functions[exec, wait, request_user_input, request_user_input_async], code mode's nested tools were apply_patch and clock__curr_time, web.run and collaboration.spawn_agent were refused as unsupported calls, no search request was sent, and exec_command was not a function. With the provider unreachable, the committed options kept retrying ('Reconnecting... waiting for network') until the probe's 60 s timeout, while the overrides ended the call in under a second with error and turn.failed events and exit 1.
isolation.source: At commit 36650394: codex-rs/features/src/lib.rs (sha256 db6dad91fd2ea65d0c976c812be325c6109e97f6275410c6cfaae2d20a5cd3f9, the file the qualification's daemon source check read) defines shell_tool, unified_exec, sleep_tool, view_image, goals, hooks, plugins, apps, multi_agent ('Enable collab tools') and unbounded_connection_retries ('Keep active sampling turns alive until a failed network connection recovers'). codex-rs/core/src/config/mod.rs chooses the sub-agent tool version from features.multi_agent_v2, then agents.enabled (default true), then the model catalog, and only then features.multi_agent, so features.multi_agent=false cannot remove the collaboration tools the catalog turns on, and agents.enabled=false does.
isolation.what_remains: Code mode's exec (JavaScript in a V8 isolate without file system, network or console; its nested tools are apply_patch, which the read-only sandbox refuses, and clock__curr_time), wait and request_user_input. The prompt asks for no tool, and any tool call fails the call (json_events.tool_detection).
isolation.evidence_class: A local loopback probe of the pinned CLI with a scripted fake provider: it shows which tools Codex offers and how it handles calls. It is not a provider run and says nothing about model behaviour.

codex.working_directory: An empty 0700 scratch directory (gt26-call-*) in the system temporary directory, outside the state tree and every repository, removed after the call; it is also the call's HOME and TMPDIR. Codex 0.157.1 reads project AGENTS.md files from the working directory up to the nearest .git ancestor, and from the working directory alone when there is none (codex-rs/core/src/agents_md.rs at the pinned commit), so no project file reaches the call, and the empty HOME hides user skills under ~/.agents/skills.
codex.codex_home: Each call's own CODEX_HOME, <attempt>/codex-home (0700), holding only a symlink auth.json to the native sign-in file (the runner's $CODEX_HOME/auth.json or ~/.codex/auth.json), which is never read or copied. --ignore-user-config skips config.toml but not $CODEX_HOME/AGENTS.md or the user's skills (tools/sota-convergence/codex_lane.py, measured with 0.155.1); a fresh home holds neither, nor any hook, config or earlier session, and Codex's session record, logs and state for the call stay in the private attempt directory. Codex's file credential store writes a refreshed token in place through the link (codex-rs/login/src/auth/storage.rs, FileAuthStorage::save opens the path with OpenOptions). The link is removed when the call ends; if Codex ever leaves a file in its place, the run stops and leaves it untouched. codex exec has no background-server code (evidence/artifacts/sota-refresh-20260926/codex/stage/daemon-source-checks.txt), and no probe case's CODEX_HOME held a daemon package.
codex.environment: Only PATH, LANG, LC_ALL, LC_CTYPE, TERM, SSL_CERT_FILE, SSL_CERT_DIR and the proxy variables pass from the runner (codex_lane.py's allowlist), plus the call's CODEX_HOME and its scratch HOME and TMPDIR. No API key variable reaches Codex, so every call uses the native sign-in, and no RUST_LOG variable, so stderr carries only Codex's default diagnostics.
codex.system_config: --ignore-user-config does not skip the system layers /etc/codex/config.toml, /etc/codex/requirements.toml and /etc/codex/managed_config.toml (codex-rs/config/src/loader/mod.rs); a run refuses to start while one exists. None existed on this host on 2026-09-26. Enterprise cloud configuration is not controlled here.
codex.schema: response.schema.json, copied once per arm into the arm's state directory and hash-checked. Codex 0.157.1 sends --output-schema as a strict json_schema text format named codex_output_schema (evidence/artifacts/sota-refresh-20260926/codex/out/provider-requests.json, requests to a loopback fake provider).
never: ultra effort (it lets Codex delegate to sub-agents, which breaks a one-model arm)
--search, or any override that turns web search, the shell or sub-agents back on
an API key in a call's environment

catalog_observation.source: codex debug models --bundled on 2026-09-26: the catalog shipped inside the codex-cli 0.157.1 binary, printed without a refresh or provider request
catalog_observation.note: The bundled catalog is the binary's own list, not the provider's live catalog. Every arm's model and effort are listed there. Under --ignore-user-config each model runs at its catalog default service tier: gpt-6-sol and gpt-6-luna default to priority, and gpt-6-astra lists no default. The frozen command does not override the tier, so wall time compares arms at their defaults.

json_events.usage: The usage object of turn.completed, summed over a call's turn.completed events: input_tokens, cached_input_tokens, cache_write_input_tokens, output_tokens and reasoning_output_tokens.
json_events.subset_rule: input_tokens includes cached_input_tokens, and output_tokens includes reasoning_output_tokens (docs/token-practice.md: 'Codex total is input plus output; cached input and reasoning are subsets'; the qualification receipt's fake-provider turn reported input 11, cached 3, output 7 and reasoning 2). analyze.py checks the rule on every call and makes the result inconclusive if any call breaks it.
json_events.usage_limit: Codex reports the account limit as an error event and a turn.failed event on stdout, whose message contains 'hit your usage limit', and exits 1 (the qualification receipt's fake-provider case). Only these two event types count. Model content (item.* events) and stderr never count: codex_job.py records that on 2026-09-26 a grep of a whole event stream matched a cited README and falsely stopped the sweep. The runner reads the stream while the call runs and publishes the LIMIT note as soon as such an event appears.
json_events.tool_detection: Codex's --json stream shows shell and web-search items but not code mode's exec cells; the session record in the call's CODEX_HOME (sessions/**/rollout-*.jsonl) lists every response item, including function_call and custom_tool_call (isolation-probe/results.json, cases committed-code-mode and isolated-code-mode). Expected items are message and reasoning in the session record, and agent_message, reasoning and error in the --json stream. Any tool item (function_call, custom_tool_call, local_shell_call or web_search_call and their outputs; command_execution, web_search, mcp_tool_call, file_change, todo_list or collab_tool_call) fails the call with reason tool_use, so no reply produced with a tool is scored. Any other item type, and a completed turn without a session record, makes the call unavailable (unexpected_item, rollout_missing): it is not scored, uses no retry and stops the arm for inspection, so an item type this plan does not know cannot spend every batch's retry.

arms.why: Today's default for every GPT-6 step on this host.
The same model with less reasoning: isolates the effort.
The catalog's workhorse model at maximum effort.
The workhorse model at its catalog default effort.
The catalog's fast and affordable model at maximum effort.
The fast and affordable model at its catalog default effort.

not_arms.reason: Never: ultra lets Codex delegate to sub-agents, which breaks a one-model arm.
Not requested. Six arms bracket each model at max and medium; a routable medium arm makes the efforts between the two unnecessary for this question.

not_arms.what: gpt-5.6 models and the other catalog entries
not_arms.reason: Out of scope: the question is routing within the GPT-6 family.

task.description: Predict the Form 8-K item codes each filing of a batch declares, from the text of its primary document.
task.reuses: blueprints/convergence-practice/local-inference-latest-20260926 (li26): its cohort, header labels, exclusions, normalized inputs and scoring functions, unchanged.

acquisition.location: sec/acq-20260926 under li26's private state directory, passed as --acquisition
acquisition.verification: li26 eval_arm.load_inputs: the SHA-256 of inputs.jsonl, a complete manifest naming that hash, and unique accessions in sorted order. li26's own verify-inputs reported 'verified 360 eligible filings' on 2026-09-26 while this plan was written.

task.labels: li26's labels: the filer-declared header ITEMS of each accession. They are not hand-checked or frontier-model labels.
task.input: li26's input for each filing, unchanged: the primary document with the whole SEC header removed, HTML reduced to text, whitespace normalized, and text over 16,000 characters cut to its first 12,000 and last 4,000.
task.privacy: SEC filings are public, so sending them to the provider is permitted. Replies, events, Codex's session records and per-call records stay in the private state directory. Filing text never enters the repository, and the decision file holds aggregates only.

batching.order: The frozen input order: accession order, as li26's load_inputs requires.
batching.rule: Greedy and order-preserving: a filing joins the current batch while the batch then holds at most 15 filings and its whole prompt stays under 110,000 UTF-8 bytes; otherwise it starts the next batch. A filing whose prompt alone reaches the bound, or whose text contains a batch delimiter or a NUL character (no argument can carry one), is refused before any call.
batching.prompt: prompt.txt with @@FILING_COUNT@@ replaced by the batch size and @@FILINGS@@ by the batch's filings, each written as <<<FILING accession="...">>>, its text, <<<END FILING accession="...">>>, separated by blank lines.
batching.argv_bound: Each prompt is one argument; Linux caps one argument at 131,072 bytes.
batching.layout_hash_input: SHA-256 of the compact JSON list of each batch's accession list, in batch order

observed_on_frozen_inputs.computed: run_arm.py layout on the verified acquisition, 2026-09-26, before any call

calls.slot_rule: Before its call, each worker takes the first free slot lock (slot-1 to slot-3) in the host's lock directory, polling every 5 s while all are held, and releases it only after the call is recorded and any stop note is published. codex inherits the slot lock and the arm's run lock, so a killed runner frees neither while its codex still runs.

call_outcomes.ok: Exit 0, a completed turn, no turn.failed event, a session record without any tool item, and a reply file whose whole text, or one markdown fence around it, parses as the response envelope.
call_outcomes.failed: The model ran and the call is unusable: a timeout, a tool item (tool_use), a non-zero exit or turn.failed after a completed turn, no reply, or a reply that is not the envelope. It counts toward the batch's retry.
call_outcomes.limit: A usage-limit error or turn.failed event. The runner publishes the LIMIT note as soon as the event appears, while the call still runs and before its slot is released; no call starts after it, running calls finish and are recorded, and the run exits 3. This is account state, not a batch failure: after the reset the batch runs again without using its retry.
call_outcomes.unavailable: No completed turn and no usage-limit event (network, sign-in, a rate limit that is not the usage limit, a server error or a failed launch), or a completed turn whose session record is missing (rollout_missing) or holds an item type this plan does not know (unexpected_item). The runner publishes the UNAVAILABLE note before the slot is released, no call starts after it, and the run exits 4. It never uses the batch's retry; after the cause is fixed (an unknown item type needs a plan amendment) and the note removed, the batch runs again.
call_outcomes.interrupted: SIGINT or SIGTERM stopped the call (TERM to its process group, KILL after 10 s). Not counted toward the retry; the run exits 5 and a later run sends the batch again.
call_outcomes.abandoned: A runner died before recording the call; the arm's next run records it from its files and removes its credential link. Not counted toward the retry, unless its events show the usage limit, which makes it a limit call whose note the next run publishes before any call.

calls.batch_states: completed: an ok call. failed: two failed calls; the batch never runs again and its filings stay in every denominator as invalid. pending: anything else; a later run of the same arm continues it.
calls.resume: A later run of the same arm keeps every recorded attempt, records attempts a dead runner left behind, publishes any usage limit such an attempt shows (and exits 3 without a call), and continues only pending batches. A run whose plan, prompt, schema, inputs, layout or Codex version differs from the arm's first run is refused.
calls.limit_note: <state dir>/LIMIT (JSON: arm, batch, attempt, time, reason and Codex's message). While it exists, every run exits 3 without a call, and an arm already running starts no further call and exits 3. The coordinator tells the user and removes it after the reset. A runner that died before publishing it leaves a limit call without a note, which the arm's next run publishes before any call; a death between publishing and recording can make that run stop once more for the same event, which costs one more removal.
calls.unavailable_note: <state dir>/UNAVAILABLE (JSON: arm, batch, attempt, time, reason and Codex's first error message). While it exists, every run exits 4 without a call, and an arm already running starts no further call and exits 4. The coordinator reads the named attempt's stderr.txt and events.jsonl, fixes the cause (sign-in, network or the service), removes it and runs the arm again.

exit_codes.0: the arm has no pending batch and no failed batch
exit_codes.2: refused before any call: a changed frozen hash, plan value, input or layout, another Codex version, a system Codex configuration file, no native sign-in file, an unsafe state or temporary directory, a missing lock directory, a run already in progress, or a run that differs from the arm's first run
exit_codes.6: the arm has no pending batch, but a batch failed twice: final for this arm; read the failure reasons before starting the next arm

calls.launch_gate: <state dir>/launch.lock, an fcntl.flock that every arm's runner holds while it checks for a stop note, prepares a call and starts it, and while it writes a stop note. Once a note exists, no call of any arm starts.

metrics.per_filing: li26's functions: precision tp/(tp+fp), 0 when nothing valid is predicted; recall tp/(tp+fn); F1 2tp/(2tp+fp+fn); exact match when the predicted set equals the declared set.
metrics.micro_f1: 2*sum(tp)/(2*sum(tp)+sum(fp)+sum(fn)) over all 360 filings, with li26's micro_f1.
metrics.macro_f1: li26's macro_f1: the mean per-code F1 over codes declared by at least 5 filings.
metrics.json_valid_rate: Share of the 360 filings whose batch's final reply is exactly the response envelope (no fence, no duplicate keys), whose accession has exactly one entry, and whose items pass li26's per-filing rule (unique strings matching [1-9].[0-9]{2}). A fenced reply is scored for F1 but is not JSON-valid. Filings of failed or pending batches are invalid and predict nothing.
metrics.tokens: Per arm, the totals and the means per filing (total / 360) over every call that reported usage, whatever its outcome (ok, failed, retried, limit, unavailable, interrupted or abandoned): input, cached input, uncached input (input - cached), cache-write input, output (which includes reasoning), reasoning, visible output (output - reasoning) and billed tokens.
metrics.billed_tokens: Uncached input plus output. The task's 'output plus reasoning' is Codex's output_tokens, which already includes reasoning_output_tokens; adding reasoning again would count it twice. Cached input is reported separately and not billed here. cache_write_input_tokens is reported and not added.
metrics.usage_completeness: A call without a usage report counts as zero only when no billed request can have run: a failed launch, or a turn refused by the usage limit. Any other call without a report (a timeout, an unavailable, interrupted or abandoned call) may have spent tokens Codex never reported, so its arm's usage is incomplete and its totals are a lower bound. The decision file lists such calls by outcome.
metrics.wall_time: Per call, from launch to exit, excluding the wait for a slot (recorded separately); per arm the median over ok calls, the total over all calls, that total per filing, the slot wait and the summed run time.
metrics.failures: Calls by outcome and reason (tool_use included), retried, failed and pending batches, unexpected entries and every record inconsistency.

decision_rule.text: An arm is routable for mechanical 8-K item extraction when (1) the paired bootstrap (10,000 resamples, seed 20260926) 95% lower bound of micro-F1(arm) - micro-F1(A0) is at least -0.02, (2) its JSON-valid rate is at least 0.98, and (3) every one of its batches completed. Cost is the mean billed tokens per filing: uncached input plus output, where Codex's output already includes reasoning. A candidate is recommended only when it is routable, its usage is complete, and its cost is strictly below A0's; among such candidates the cheapest wins, ties going to the lower median wall time of its ok calls, then to plan order. Otherwise the default (A0) stays. If A0's usage is incomplete, its reported cost is a lower bound: a candidate below it is still recommended, and if a ranked candidate exists but none is below it, the result is inconclusive. Cached input, reasoning and quota percentages are reported separately, and quota percentages never enter the rule.

bootstrap.method: li26's paired_bootstrap, unchanged: filings in accession order; each resample is random.Random(20260926).choices over the filing indices, applied to both arms, and micro-F1 is recomputed for each.
bootstrap.lower_bound: Nearest-rank 2.5th percentile: the 250th smallest of the 10,000 differences.

decision_rule.every_batch_completed: The arm has no pending and no failed batch, and its record has no inconsistency: attempt numbers, identities, prompt hashes, usage re-read from the events, and reply status all agree.
decision_rule.cost_comparison: Strictly below A0: the question asks for A0's quality at lower token cost, so a tie with A0 keeps the default. A0 is the reference and never a ranked candidate. A candidate whose usage is incomplete is not ranked: its true cost may be higher than reported.
decision_rule.control_validity: If A0 has not run, the outcome is inconclusive_control_not_evaluated. While any A0 batch is pending, it is inconclusive_control_incomplete. If A0 has a failed batch, a record inconsistency or a JSON-valid rate below 0.98, it is inconclusive_control_invalid. If A0's usage is incomplete and a ranked candidate exists but none costs less than A0's reported (lower-bound) cost, it is inconclusive_control_usage_incomplete. No routing changes in any of these cases.
decision_rule.subset_guard: If any call reports cached input above input, or reasoning above output, the billed-token definition does not hold; the outcome is inconclusive_usage_subset_rule_violated.

outcomes.route_mechanical_extraction: A candidate is selected: route mechanical extraction stages to its model and effort.
outcomes.keep_default: The default stays, with reason no_routable_candidate, no_candidate_with_known_usage or no_candidate_below_control.

decision_rule.final: The decision file marks final true only when all six arms are complete (no pending batch).
decision_rule.frozen_code: analyze.py verifies every frozen input against frozen_inputs before it reads anything and records that map in the decision file, so changed analysis or scoring code is refused.

quota_context.caveat: Percentages of the shared weekly Codex allowance read before and after an arm are context only. Other sessions share the account, so a percentage change is not attributable to one arm, and it never enters the rule.
quota_context.input: Optional: analyze.py --quota-context FILE, where FILE is {"source": ..., "readings": [{"arm", "window", "before_percent", "after_percent", "before_utc", "after_utc"}]} as the coordinator read them.

failure_rule: Retain every call: ok, failed, limit, unavailable, interrupted and abandoned. A failed batch runs once more and never again. A limit, unavailable, interrupted or abandoned call never counts as a batch failure; its batch runs again after the reset, the fix or the restart. No re-run of a completed or failed batch, and no changed model, effort, prompt, schema, batching or command. Changing any frozen value needs a new plan.
state_dir: ~/.local/state/native-agent-stack/gpt6-family-tiering-20260926/: 0700 directories and 0600 files. It holds launch.lock, LIMIT or UNAVAILABLE when present, and arms/<arm>/ with identity.json, schema.json, run.lock, runs.jsonl and batches/<batch>/attempt-<n>/ (events.jsonl, stderr.txt, reply.json, call.json, and codex-home/ with Codex's session record, logs and state for that call; its auth.json link exists only while the call runs). Each call's scratch HOME, TMPDIR and working directory are created in the system temporary directory and removed after the call.
planning_estimate: Not a measurement. The 25 prompts of one arm total 2,016,724 bytes, which at about 4 bytes per token is roughly 0.5 million input tokens per arm before Codex's own instructions, which are sent with every call. Reasoning at max effort adds output. Six arms therefore spend a few million tokens of the shared allowance.
claims_excluded: frontier parity, or accuracy against hand-checked labels
any stage other than mechanical extraction with a deterministic scorer
catalyst, incentive or trading-signal value of item codes
provider cost in money, or a percentage of the weekly allowance attributable to one arm
token savings of a whole task or workflow
stability over time, other days, other batch sizes or other Codex versions
isolated latency: calls share a host, an account and provider load, and sol and luna run at their priority default tier
tokens a call spent that Codex never reported: a call without a usage report makes its arm's totals a lower bound
behaviour of the command without the isolation overrides, or of a stage that lets the model use tools
